quote.quote: This application was referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) for review because of the considerable evidence of hepatotoxicity in the premarketing setting and because of its status as a new molecular entity.
The ODAC meeting was held on October 5, 2009.

recommendation.text: The committee voted 10 to 0 (Yes=10, No=0, Abstain=0) that the benefit-to-risk profile of pazopanib was acceptable for the treatment of patients with advanced RCC.

quote.quote: The committee voted 10 to 0 that benefit to risk profile was acceptable.

linkages.concern: Committee members raised concerns about the potential liver toxicity (hepatotoxicity) signal seen in the premarketing data and strongly recommended post-market monitoring of this signal if the drug were approved.
linkages.change: FDA issued post-marketing requirements focused on the liver safety signal, including a report on the safety of pazopanib dose modification and rechallenge in patients with elevated ALT and a final report of the ongoing hepatic impairment trial.

concern_quote.quote: The committee members expressed concerns about the potential liver toxicity signal and strongly recommended post-market monitoring of this possible signal if approved.

change_quote.quote: Submit a report, from several ongoing trials, concerning the safety of pazopanib dose modification and rechallenge in patients with elevated ALT.

linkages.concern: Committee members raised concerns about the potential liver toxicity (hepatotoxicity) signal observed in the premarketing data.
linkages.change: Hepatotoxicity was included as a boxed warning in the pazopanib label, accompanied by a Medication Guide, to better inform practitioners and patients about the risks of pazopanib.

summary: An Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held on October 5, 2009; the application was referred to ODAC because of considerable premarketing evidence of hepatotoxicity and the drug's status as a new molecular entity. The committee voted 10-0 that pazopanib's benefit-to-risk profile was acceptable for advanced RCC, but members expressed concern about the potential liver toxicity signal and strongly recommended post-market monitoring. Votrient was approved with a hepatotoxicity boxed warning and Medication Guide and with liver-safety post-marketing requirements, though the review documents do not explicitly state these changes were made in direct response to the committee.
